Subject: POC: Capacity planning and success criteria (VenturoTech)

Hi Samir / Priya 

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned on the POC scope and capacity plan.

Objective / success criteria (proposed)
- Reduce latency for conversational assistant calls to p95 <= 350ms for single-turn web chat flows.
- Sustained throughput: support 1,200 requests/minute during peak test windows.
- Functional: model responses match your 10 canonical prompts with >90% accept rate in manual review.
- Instrumentation: telemetry events (latency, tokens, error rate) available to Venturo for every request.

Evaluation plan / timeline
- Week 0 (this week): finalize success criteria and sign MAA (mutual action plan).
- Week 1: provision infra + integration (SDK keys, sample dataset, telemetry hooks).
- Week 2: run baseline tests (low concurrency) and tune batching/kv-cache.
- Week 3: peak concurrency validation and cost run; handoff for decision.

POC capacity proposal (initial)
- Reserved baseline: 2 x A100 GPUs (reserved) to ensure stable cold-start behavior and dedicated throughput.
- Autoscale / burst: allow burst up to 8 x A100 for short windows (4 hours) during peak load tests.
- Autoscaling policy: scale by queue length and token/sec, target p95 latency <= 350ms, cooldown 90s.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (expected to reduce token cost by ~20-30%).

Ownership / contacts
- Redwood PM / primary: Marissa Cole (me)  program lead for POC logistics.
- Redwood SRE / infra: Nikhil Sharma  provisioning, autoscale config.
- SE / evaluation: Rishi Malhotra  eval scripts, quality checks.
- Venturo contact: Samir Gupta  product lead; Priya Kapoor  engineering.

Attachments: venturotech_poc_capacity_estimate.xlsx (capacity + cost estimate), redwood_poc_playbook.docx (integration checklist).

Next steps
1) Please confirm the success criteria above or suggest edits by EOD Thu.
2) Confirm PO or MSA path for sandbox provisioning (contracts contact if needed).
3) If agreed, we’ll provision baseline reserved GPUs by Mon and aim to kick off integration next Tue.

Thanks  looking forward to moving fast.

Best,
Marissa

Marissa  thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side before we lock things in: 

1) Concurrency profile: the 1,200 req/minute peak is for our web chat flows. Are those single-turn requests or multi-turn sessions (KV cache behavior will differ)? We expect a mix but about 60% single-turn.
2) Burst behavior: we need to understand cold-start implications when bursting from 2 to 8 GPUs  specifically how long to reach steady-state and any warm-up guidance.
3) Cost sensitivity: procurement will want a cap on burst hours for the POC. Can you provide a burn estimate for the proposed 4-hour burst?

Success criteria look good; we’d add an acceptance item: automated test run with the 10 canonical prompts and a pass rate threshold documented in the playbook.

Procurement / contracting: looped in contracts@venturotech.com for the sandbox order path.

If you can answer the three items above, we can confirm and get our infra team to schedule integration.

Samir

Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC: Capacity planning and success criteria (VenturoTech)

Thanks Samir  good questions. Answers inline: 

1) Concurrency profile: Plan assumes mix with ~60% single-turn. Our autoscaler and KV cache settings will treat session state as ephemeral unless you opt to persist longer. For the POC we’ll instrument session ids and keep KV cache TTL at 30 minutes to maximize cache hits for repeated prompts. That should help single-turn latency significantly.

2) Burst cold-starts: With 2 reserved GPUs we maintain a warm pool for fast routing. Bursting to 8 uses a combination of predictive pre-warm and container start parallelism. Expected time to steady state: ~90180s depending on model tokenization and pipeline. We’ll run a short warm-up script (included in the playbook) before peak windows to reduce that to ~60s.

3) Burn estimate: attached spreadsheet has a conservative cost estimate for a single 4-hour burst (8 GPUs) at current market rates — see "burst_cost_scenarios" tab. For the POC we recommend a soft cap of 12 total burst hours; we can auto-notify Venturo when usage exceeds 8 hours.

Playbook updates: I’ve added your acceptance item (automated canonical prompt test) to the playbook and linked the test harness under related links.

Proposed provisioning plan: reserve baseline by Mon (2xA100), provisioning window 2448 hours. Kickoff integration Tue.

Ownership reminder: Nikhil will provision infra; Rishi will own eval scripts and pass/fail criteria. Dev / Redwood sales will coordinate contracts and PO path.

Let us know if procurement needs a formal SOW or a simple sandbox order form.

Best,
Marissa

Samir / team  Nikhil here (SRE). Quick infra notes for the POC provisioning: 

- Reserved baseline: 2 x A100 (NVMe-backed, pre-pulled container images).
- Autoscale policy: scale up when request queue > 200 or CPU/GPU utilization > 65% for 45s; scale down when utilization < 40% for 90s. Max burst cap: 8 x A100.
- Pre-warm: we will run the "prewarm.sh" warm-up (included in playbook) 10 minutes before scheduled peak windows. That reduces cold-start to ~60s in tests.
- Burst expectations: we can sustain 8 GPUs for up to 4 hours without manual approval; beyond that we’ll send a billing notification and require a manual opt-in.
- Telemetry: we’ll emit Prometheus metrics + request-level traces to the shared sandbox project and provide a Grafana dashboard.

Cost / logging: see attached cost worksheet for per-hour estimates. For procurement: we can generate a short PO-friendly estimate doc if contracts need it.

I’ll take point on provisioning once Marissa confirms the PO path.

Nikhil
